subject: Effective date backfill, billing/pricing question, and SOW redlines
messages:

Our procurement team flagged two items: 1) a brief SOW paragraph to capture pilot scope (30 days, internal-only test) and 2) confirmation that any retroactive credits will be applied as an invoice credit (not a refund).

Can you confirm next steps and whether Redwood legal needs to redline the effective date or create a separate change order?

— Ava

Ava — thanks for the note and congrats on getting the pilot running early. Short answers:
- We can accommodate an effective-date backfill to 2027-05-01.
- Retroactive billing is doable as an invoice credit applied to your next invoice.
- We should capture the pilot scope in a short SOW paragraph (Exhibit A). Legal will need to approve a redline to the order form that sets the effective date and adds the pilot paragraph — this can be a change order (amendment) or an updated order form with a single redline, whichever the LumaHealth procurement team prefers.

Looping in Laura (account lead) to confirm commercial terms and Karthik (legal) for redlines. Laura — any commercial caveats? Karthik — can you take the lead on a minimal redline that: 1) changes effective date, 2) adds a one-paragraph pilot scope in Exhibit A, and 3) confirms invoice credit treatment? I attached the current order form and Exhibit A for reference.

Next steps / ask list:
- Karthik: provide redline and short cover note for procurement.
- Laura: confirm the credit amount will show as a line credit on next invoice, and confirm DocuSign routing (single signer at LumaHealth or procurement + legal?).
- Ava / LumaHealth: confirm you want a single amended order form or a standalone change order.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Diego

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Ava Mills <ava.mills@lumahealth.com>, procurement@lumahealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form / SOW questions

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the docs quickly and propose the following approach to minimize legal friction:

- Create a short amendment/change order that:
  * States: "The Order Form effective date is amended to May 1, 2027 for the Services defined in Exhibit A (Pilot)."
  * Attaches a one-paragraph Exhibit A addendum describing pilot scope/duration and non-production restrictions.
  * Specifies: "Any amounts invoiced for the pilot period shall be credited on the subsequent invoice as a line-item credit."

- Rationale: procurement teams prefer a discrete amendment for retroactive changes (clear audit trail), and it avoids re-issuing the entire order form.
- Impact: no change to MSA; no new indemnities or data residency changes.
- Ask: Confirm the pilot credit amount or the mechanism (estimated usage x negotiated pilot rate) so finance can calculate the credit line.

I prepared a redline draft and attached it as OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx. It contains: the amendment cover language, the brief Exhibit A paragraph, and an explicit billing credit line. I also added a small clause clarifying acceptance criteria for the pilot (internal test only; no SLA during pilot).

If LumaHealth wants the consolidated approach (updated order form rather than amendment), we can do that too — functionally equivalent but slightly messier for audit teams.

Pls review the attached redline and tell me whether to proceed with an amendment (recommended) or consolidated order form. If approved, I'll send a DocuSign envelope and include the standard signatory block for both Redwood and LumaHealth.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx
From: Ava Mills <ava.mills@lumahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form / SOW questions

Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. Procurement prefers a discrete amendment (audit reasons). A couple of clarifications from our finance team:
- Credit calculation: use actual pilot usage (token/embedding units billed) multiplied by the agreed pilot rate per unit. We can provide the usage report for May; can you confirm which report / fields you need?
- Acceptance clause: okay with internal-only pilot (no SLA) but we need the clause to explicitly say Redwood will not invoice production-scale features under pilot pricing.

If you can update the redline to reference "invoice credit to be applied to the invoice following execution of this Amendment" and include a short list of the usage fields (date range, token_count, embedding_count, line_item_id) that would be ideal. Once we have the updated redline we'll route to our legal and procurement for signature.

We prefer DocuSign with a single LumaHealth signatory from procurement (legal will countersign if any material changes).

— Ava
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Order form / SOW questions

Thanks everyone — Karthik updated the redline per Ava's requests and I attached the new file to the DocuSign envelope. Summary of what was included in the amendment (for the record):
- Effective date amended to 2027-05-01 for the pilot scope described in Exhibit A addendum.
- Exhibit A addendum: one paragraph capturing pilot duration (05/01/2027 — 05/30/2027), internal-only test, and features included.
- Billing credit: explicit statement that usage during the pilot period will be credited on the invoice immediately following execution; calculation uses reported token_count and embedding_count fields.
- Acceptance: pilot is non-production; no SLA during pilot.

Action items / next steps:
1) Ava / procurement: please sign the DocuSign envelope at https://app.docusign.com/ABC1234567890 (envelope sent).
2) LumaHealth finance: please send the usage report for May (CSV preferred) to billing@redwood.com — include date range and token_count / embedding_count.
3) Finance / Billing at Redwood: once usage received, we will compute the credit and apply to next invoice; Laura to confirm credit line on invoice.

If anyone wants a 15-minute sync to walk through the amendment, I can be available this afternoon or tomorrow morning.

— Diego
